QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_5

question.text: Mr. Arjun Mehra, a first-time LP, is evaluating three investment routes: (i) a Category I VC Fund, (ii) a Category I Angel Fund, and (iii) a Category II Private Debt Fund. All three are ordinary (non-LVF, non-Accredited-Investor) schemes. According to the SEBI (AIF) Regulations as described in Chapter 3, what is the minimum investor commitment per investor for the Category I VC Fund?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Comparison table in Chapter 3, investors in Category I AIFs must invest a minimum of INR 1 crore. This applies to a standard Category I VCF. The footnote to the table notes that this minimum is 'Not applicable to Angel Funds and Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors', i.e., Angel Funds have a lower INR 25 lakh threshold at the angel-investor level but the general Cat I/II investor floor is INR 1 crore. The Trap: INR 10 lakh and INR 25 lakh are thresholds that apply to Angel Fund investments (minimum INR 25 lakh in a particular investee, and ticket size constraints are different). INR 5 crore is the minimum for a Large Value Fund (LVF) for Accredited Investors, which is a separate regime. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A and XIX-C test the same INR 1 crore floor. Accredited Investor and LVF relaxations are tested more intensively in XIX-C. Cat III AIFs (XIX-E) have the same INR 1 crore investor minimum, but this question deliberately focuses on Cat I/II. Manager's Pro-Tip: When a Cat I/II manager is marketing to first-time LPs, always include the INR 1 crore floor on the first page of the teaser — Distributors and private bankers often overlook it and onboard INR 50 lakh tickets, which SEBI treats as a Regulation 10 breach during inspection.
